questions.question_text: A basketball player scored $23$, $16$, $31$, $19$ and $27$ points in five games. What is the range of the number of points?

options.why: Subtracted the second-smallest score $19$ from the maximum instead of subtracting the minimum.
Gave the maximum score instead of the difference between the maximum and the minimum.
Gave the minimum score instead of the difference between the maximum and the minimum.

questions.question_text: A netball shooter scored $18$, $22$, $15$, $22$, $20$ and $18$ goals in six games. What is the mode?

options.why: Stopped at the first repeated value instead of reporting every value that ties for most frequent.
Chose the larger of the two repeated values, but $18$ occurs twice as well.
Calculated the median of the ordered data instead of the most frequent value.

questions.question_text: A basketball player scored $21$, $14$, $18$, $9$, $16$, $11$ and $13$ points in seven games. What is the mean, correct to $1$ decimal place?

options.why: Rounded $14.57$ down instead of up to $1$ decimal place.
Divided the total $102$ by $6$ instead of by the $7$ data values.
Gave the median of the ordered data instead of the mean.

questions.question_text: A netball shooter scored $26$, $19$, $31$, $23$, $28$ and $21$ goals in six games. What is the median?

options.why: Took the lower of the two middle scores instead of the mean of the two.
Took the upper of the two middle scores instead of the mean of the two.
Averaged the two middle values of the unsorted list without ordering the data first.

questions.question_text:
The $15$ scores below are the points a basketball team scored in each game of a season, listed in ascending order.
$34, 37, 39, 41, 44, 46, 49, 52, 55, 58, 60, 63, 67, 70, 75$
Using $\text{Position} = \frac{n+1}{2}$, what is the median?

options.why: Found position $8$ correctly but counted from zero, reading the $9$th score.
Halved $n$ instead of $n+1$ and read the $7$th score.
Gave the position of the median instead of the score sitting at that position.

questions.question_text: A basketball player's points in six games were $20$, $14$, $17$, $14$, $23$ and $18$. Which line gives all four summary statistics correctly, with the mean written correct to $1$ decimal place?

options.why: Took the lower of the two middle scores, $17$, as the median instead of averaging the two middle scores $17$ and $18$.
Quoted the largest score, $23$, as the range instead of subtracting the smallest from the largest.
Quoted the largest score as the range and also took the lower middle score $17$ as the median rather than averaging $17$ and $18$.
Read the repeated leaf digit instead of combining it with its stem to give the whole value.
Chose the first repeated value in the plot instead of the value that occurs most often.
Gave the median, the middle value of the nine scores, instead of the most frequent value.

questions.solution_text:
$35, 38, 38, 42, 46, 51, 51, 51, 54$
$51$ occurs three times and every other value occurs at most twice.
$\text{Mode} = 51$

options.why: Took the lower of the two middle values instead of the mean of the two.
Averaged the third and fourth columns as they stand on the graph without ordering the data.
Gave the mode, the value read from two equal columns, instead of the median.

questions.question_text: A basketball player's points in six games, in ascending order, are $9$, $12$, $16$, $x$, $24$ and $28$. The median is $19$. What is the value of $x$?

options.why: Assumed the missing score must equal the median rather than solving for it.
Doubled the median but forgot to subtract the other middle score $16$.
Subtracted $16$ from the median instead of from twice the median.

questions.question_text: Five of a netball shooter's game scores are shown in ascending order: $11$, $p$, $q$, $r$, $27$. The mean, median and mode of the five scores are all $17$. Which values complete the list?

options.why: Uses the right three values but breaks the stated ascending order of the list.
Splits the remaining total evenly, which makes $15$ the mode instead of $17$.
Satisfies the mean and median but leaves only one $17$, so there is no mode of $17$.

questions.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = \frac{11 + p + q + r + 27}{5}$
$17 = \frac{38 + p + q + r}{5}$
$85 = 38 + p + q + r$
$p + q + r = 47$
The median is the $3$rd score, so $q = 17$ and $p + r = 30$.
The mode is $17$, so a second $17$ is needed among $p$ and $r$; the remaining value is then $30 - 17 = 13$, and ascending order puts it first.
$p = 13$, $q = 17$, $r = 17$
